_readme: Inputs to research/manuscripts/emc_mortality_decomposition.py. Every survival figure here is a READING of research/data/emc-clinical-registry.json, which is its one home (CLAUDE.md rule 1) -- this file does not own a single clinical number. `registry_verbatim` is the exact string the value was read out of, and the script FAILS if that string is no longer present in the registry at the stated path, so a registry correction cannot silently leave a stale figure in the decomposition. The registry stores several of these as free text ('82/65/58% (5/10/15-yr OS)'), which is why the extraction is declared here explicitly rather than parsed by a regex that would quietly mis-read a reformatted string.

series.label: Meis-Kindblom 1999 pathology series
series.pairing_note: The only series in the registry that reports BOTH a long-horizon all-cause survival curve and a disease-specific death count on the same patients. The two are not on the same estimator -- 70% is a survival-curve reading at 10 years, 18/99 is a crude proportion over a median 108-month follow-up -- so the within-series decomposition below is approximate and is reported as such. It is still the only decomposition that does not cross populations.

series.label: Drilon 2008 two-referral-centre series
series.pairing_note: All-cause only. Contributes the all-cause side of the cross-series pairing; it reports no disease-specific figure, so nothing is inferred about ITS cause split.

series.label: Japanese multi-institutional series
series.pairing_note: The most favourable all-cause curve in the registry and the reason the cross-series band has a wide upper edge. A 5-year all-cause survival of 100% in 42 patients means this cohort had neither an EMC death nor a background death in five years, which is a strong selection signal, not a natural-history reading.

series.label: SEER 2004-2015 population series
series.pairing_note: The largest EMC survival dataset and the least selected, so its 5-year all-cause figure is the one a population claim should lean on. SEER records survival but not recurrence.

series.label: Japanese national registry, localised surgical
series.registry_verbatim: eight (6.3%) died from tumors, and four (3.1%) died from other causes
series.pairing_note: ⭐ The cleanest pairing in this file. Both cause counts come from the same patients under the same ascertainment, so the competing share is a ratio of two counts rather than a subtraction of percentages from different studies. Localised stratum: 9 tumour deaths (8 in the no-chemotherapy arm plus 1 in the chemotherapy arm) and 4 other-cause deaths, over a median 38 months.

series.label: Japanese national registry, metastatic at diagnosis
series.registry_verbatim: five (31.3%) died of the tumors, and one (6.3%) died of other causes
series.pairing_note: Same study, advanced stratum: 9 tumour deaths (5 in the advanced-chemotherapy arm plus 4 in the arm that did not receive it) and 1 other-cause death. ⚠ The competing share is much lower here than in the localised stratum, and that is exactly what it should be -- these patients are dying of EMC faster, so the disease outruns their other causes.

series.label: MD Anderson localised series
series.pairing_note: The registry's only 10-year disease-specific figure, and therefore the disease-specific side of the headline 10-year decomposition. Localised at diagnosis, single institution.

pooled_reference.note: The registry's pooled 10-year disease-specific figure, independent of Bishop 2019's single-institution 85% and numerically equal to it. Agreement between a pooled estimate and one institution's series is reassuring but is not two independent measurements -- the pooled figure may include that series.

background_mortality._readme: Closed 2026-08-09. The question this answers is whether the observed non-EMC deaths are the SIZE an ordinary cohort of this age and sex produces anyway. A figure far ABOVE background would mean the decomposition is a study-comparability artifact rather than a reading of how patients die, and would make every competing-share number in this file unquotable. ⚠ The check is ONE-SIDED by construction: a general-population table over-states background mortality for a cohort fit enough to reach and survive a sarcoma diagnosis, so it can refute 'this gap is background' and cannot prove it.
background_mortality.cohort_age_basis: registry overview.typicalPatient: 'Most often diagnosed in adults in their 50s-60s'
background_mortality.cohort_sex_basis: registry overview.typicalPatient: 'Slight male predominance (~2:1 in several series)'
background_mortality.life_table_source: WHO Global Health Observatory, indicator LIFE_0000000029, USA, 2021
background_mortality.life_table_indicator_name_as_published: nMx - age-specific death rate between ages x and x+n
background_mortality.blended_annual_rate_derivation: 0.66 x male nMx(55-59) 0.011437434 + 0.34 x female nMx(55-59) 0.006786214. ⛔ nMx is a RATE, not a probability -- the first implementation of this fetch used it as a five-year probability and published a ten-year mortality four times too low. The indicator name above is now read from the API rather than recalled.
